title: Mirror Every Word
statement:
You get a sentence s: words separated by exactly one space, with no space at the start or end. A word is any run of non-space characters, so it may contain digits or punctuation.

Return a new string where the characters of every word are reversed, but the words stay in their original order and the single spaces stay where they were.

examples.why: Each word is flipped on its own. The order map, filter, reduce is unchanged.
Reversing the whole string would give "cb a", which also moves the words. Only letters inside a word move.
Punctuation is part of the word, so "!" travels with it.

constraints: Words are separated by exactly one space; no leading or trailing space
hints: The spaces never move. Only the characters between two spaces change places.
Find where each word starts and ends. Inside that range, what does reversing look like?
Turn the string into a character array. For each word, swap its first and last characters and move both pointers inward until they meet.

explain.intuition:
The spaces act as fixed walls. Every word is a separate little array, and reversing an array in place is the classic two-pointer swap: swap the ends, step both pointers inward, stop when they cross.

JavaScript strings are immutable, so copy the string into an array of characters first, reverse each word inside that array, and join it back at the end. That keeps the work O(n) instead of building many temporary strings.
steps: Walk with start at the beginning of a word. Move end forward until it hits a space or the end of the array.
Reverse c[start..end − 1] with two pointers that swap and move inward.
Set start = end + 1 (skip the space) and repeat until the array is done.
pitfalls: Reversing the whole sentence. That also reverses the word order.
Forgetting the last word: it ends at the end of the string, not at a space.
Building the result with repeated string concatenation inside a nested loop, which can be quadratic in some engines.

solutions.title: Split, reverse, join
solutions.idea: Split on spaces, reverse each word's characters, and join with single spaces.

solutions.title: Two pointers per word
solutions.idea: Work on a character array. For each word, swap its ends and move inward.

followups: Words may now be separated by several spaces, and those runs must be kept exactly. Does your code still work?
Reverse the order of the words instead, keeping each word's letters as they are. Can you do it with two reversal passes?
